title: OpenAI Partners with Cisco to Open Source Shirudo: A Round-the-Clock Bulletproof Vest for AI Agent Systems

content_html:
The gap between when a vulnerability is exposed and when a patch lands has always been the most painful time in the security world—systems either grit their teeth and run unprotected, or go offline and wait for a fix. OpenAI's answer on November 24 was to team up with Cisco to launch an open source project called Shirudo: an open source Linux runtime environment that lets AI agents protect systems directly without any downtime.

Shirudo's core technical approach is to have AI agents write dynamic eBPF protection rules—eBPF is a Linux kernel technology that can dynamically inject security logic without modifying the kernel or restarting the system, making it a natural fit for defending systems while they keep running. The agents use it to generate rules that defend against attacks targeting system vulnerabilities, buying security teams a valuable window to calmly test and officially deploy patches. In other words, when an attack arrives, the first line of defense is built immediately by AI, while humans slowly put up the permanent fortifications behind it.

The two companies are clear about what it is meant to be: the first step toward infrastructure with autonomous defense capabilities—adapting to new threats while keeping business operations running. OpenAI describes the ideal collaboration as follows: security staff and AI agents work together, with the agents locating affected systems, testing and sharing protection strategies, and ultimately deploying them, all without disrupting running workloads. When patches are not yet in place and attacks are already at the door, this open source solution jointly built by Cisco and OpenAI is like holding up an umbrella that will not be pulled away for servers around the world targeted by vulnerabilities.
